title: Inside an AI System
subject: AI-Literacy
description: Input, Processing and Output: the three parts of an AI system, how Google Lens sorts its jobs among them, upgrading Lens for Indian plants and food, designing your own AI with failure modes, and the 2018 medical-AI 'shortcut learning' case study.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Which three parts make up an AI system, according to the chapter?
options: Input, Processing, Output
Camera, Screen, Battery
Reading, Writing, Speaking
Training, Testing, Selling
questions.explanation: The chapter describes every AI system as three parts: Input receives information, Processing analyses it, and Output delivers the result.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: What is the job of the Input part?
options: Store the final answer for many years
Receive information from the outside world
Analyse information using learned patterns
Deliver the result so the user understands it
questions.explanation: Input receives information from the outside world and sends it on to Processing. Analysing is Processing's job and delivering results is Output's job.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Which part analyses the input using patterns learned from training data?
options: Training
Input
Processing
Output
questions.explanation: Processing analyses the input using patterns it learned from training data. Input only receives information and Output only presents the result.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Which part delivers the result in a way the user can understand?
options: Input
Processing
Camera
Output
questions.explanation: The Output part delivers the result in a way the user can understand, for example by showing a name on the screen.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: After the Input part receives information, where does it send it?
options: To the Processing part
Straight to the Output
Back to the user's eyes
To the camera's memory
questions.explanation: The worksheet says Input receives information and sends it to Processing, which then analyses it before Output shows a result.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: In the chapter's upgrade table, which part is described as 'how the AI thinks about the input'?
options: Input
Processing
Output
Feedback
questions.explanation: The table describes Processing as 'how the AI thinks about the input'. Input is 'what information enters AI' and Output is 'what the user sees at the end'.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: 'What information enters AI' describes which part?
options: Processing
Output
Input
Training data
questions.explanation: Information entering the AI is the Input part's job. Processing thinks about that information and Output shows the result.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: 'What the user sees at the end' describes which part?
options: Processing
Patterns
Input
Output
questions.explanation: What the user sees at the end is the Output. Input happens at the start and Processing happens in the middle.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: The Processing part uses patterns it learned from training data.
questions.explanation: Yes. Processing analyses the input by using patterns learned from training data, such as millions of example images.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: The Output part is the part that receives information from the outside world.
questions.explanation: False. Receiving information from the outside world is the Input part's job. Output delivers the result to the user.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Information in an AI system flows Input → Processing → Output.
questions.explanation: True. Input receives information and sends it to Processing; Processing analyses it; Output delivers the result to the user.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: The Input part decides what the information means before passing it on.
questions.explanation: False. Input only receives information and passes it on. Deciding what the information means (for example, what a photo contains) is Processing's job.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that correctly describe parts of an AI system.
options: Processing receives photos from the camera
Output trains the AI on new data
Input receives information from the outside world
Processing delivers the result on the screen
Output presents the result so the user understands it
questions.explanation: Input receives information and Output presents the result. Processing analyses, it does not display results or receive camera photos, and no part 'trains' during use.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: A student says 'the Processing part shows the answer on screen.' What is the mistake?
options: Showing the answer is the Output part's job
Showing the answer is the Input part's job
Processing never uses any training data
There is no mistake; that is correct
questions.explanation: Processing analyses and decides; showing the answer on screen is the Output part's job. Input receives information and Processing does use training data.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Which ordering shows how information moves through an AI system?
options: Output → Processing → Input
Input → Processing → Output
Processing → Input → Output
Input → Output → Processing
questions.explanation: Information enters through Input, is analysed by Processing, and is delivered by Output. The other orders would show a result before it is analysed.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Where do the patterns used by the Processing part come from?
options: From the screen that shows results
From the camera's flash settings
From the training data it learned from
From the user's typed instructions
questions.explanation: Processing analyses input 'using patterns learned from training data'. The screen, camera and user instructions do not supply those patterns.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: The chapter title is 'Inside an AI System'. What does 'inside' refer to here?
options: The metal box the computer is kept in
The person who owns the AI product
The internet cables under the ocean
The three parts and the jobs each does
questions.explanation: Looking 'inside' an AI system means understanding its three parts, Input, Processing and Output, and the specific job each part does.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Processing and Output are two names for the same part of an AI system.
questions.explanation: False. They are different parts: Processing analyses the input using learned patterns, while Output delivers the result to the user.

questions.topic: The Three Parts of an AI System
questions.question: Which part would be described as the 'thinking' part of an AI system?
options: Processing
Input
Output
Battery
questions.explanation: The upgrade table calls Processing 'how the AI thinks about the input'. Input brings information in and Output shows the result.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: In Google Lens, which job belongs to the Input part?
options: Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Capture the photograph from the camera
Compare the image to millions of examples
Show the identified object name on screen
questions.explanation: Capturing the photograph is how information enters the system, so it is an Input job. Comparing and scoring are Processing; showing the name is Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: 'Make sure the image is clear enough to use' is a job of which part?
options: Output
Processing
Input
Training
questions.explanation: Checking that the captured image is clear enough happens while receiving the information, so it belongs to Input.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: 'Pass the image data to the next part' belongs to which part?
options: Processing
Output
Display
Input
questions.explanation: Input receives the information and sends it to Processing, so passing the image data to the next part is an Input job.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Why does the Input part check that the image is clear enough?
options: So Processing gets usable information to analyse
So the user can save the photo in a gallery
So the screen can show the result more brightly
So the AI can skip the Processing step
questions.explanation: Processing can only find patterns in information it can actually use. A clear image gives Processing a fair chance to analyse it correctly.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: In Google Lens, capturing the photograph from the camera is an Input job.
questions.explanation: True. The photograph is the information coming in from the outside world, which is exactly what Input receives.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: In Google Lens, the Input part identifies patterns like shape and colour.
questions.explanation: False. Identifying patterns such as shape, colour, texture or text is a Processing job. Input only captures and passes on the image.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Select the TWO Google Lens jobs that belong to the Input part.
options: Provide links to more information
Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Capture the photograph from the camera
Pass the image data to the next part
Decide what the photograph contains
questions.explanation: Capturing the photo and passing the data on are Input jobs. Deciding contents and scoring guesses are Processing; providing links is Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Which of these Google Lens jobs does NOT belong to the Input part?
options: Pass the image data to the next part
Decide what the photograph contains
Capture the photograph from the camera
Make sure the image is clear enough to use
questions.explanation: Deciding what the photograph contains means analysing it, which is Processing. The other three are all about receiving and passing on the image.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: A phone's microphone picks up a spoken question for a voice assistant. Which part is doing this job?
options: Output
Feedback
Input
Processing
questions.explanation: The microphone receives information (sound) from the outside world, so it plays the Input role, just like the camera does in Google Lens.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: After Google Lens captures a photo, what does the Input part do next with it?
options: Displays the result on the screen
Compares it to millions of examples
Provides links to more information
Passes the image data to Processing
questions.explanation: Input receives information and sends it to Processing. Comparing is Processing's job and displaying or linking is Output's job.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: If the Input part sends a blurry, unclear photo, Processing can still be sure of the right answer.
questions.explanation: False. Processing depends on usable information. That is why Input's job includes making sure the image is clear enough to use.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: What does the Input part receive, in general?
options: Information from the outside world
Patterns from the training data
The finished result for the user
Links to more web information
questions.explanation: Input receives information from the outside world. Patterns belong to Processing and results and links belong to Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: A smart doorbell's camera records a visitor's face. In the three-part model, which part is this?
options: Output, because it shows a picture
Input, because it receives information
Processing, because it uses a camera
Processing, because it recognises faces
questions.explanation: Recording the face is receiving information from the outside world, so it is Input. Recognising who it is would be Processing, and showing an alert would be Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Which sentence best describes the Input part's role in Google Lens?
options: It writes the answer for the reader
It learns from millions of examples
It gets the photo and hands it on
It picks the best guess and scores it
questions.explanation: Input captures the photo and passes it to Processing. Picking and scoring a guess is Processing; writing the answer for the reader is Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Which is an Input-part problem rather than a Processing problem?
options: The AI was trained on too few Indian plants
The result is shown in a language the user can't read
The confidence score is too low to trust
The camera lens is dirty, so the photo is blurry
questions.explanation: A dirty lens affects the information coming in, so it is an Input problem. Too little training data and low confidence are Processing issues; an unreadable result is Output.

questions.topic: Input: Receiving Information
questions.question: Which device most often does the Input job in Google Lens?
options: The phone camera
The phone speaker
The phone screen
The phone battery
questions.explanation: Google Lens receives its information as a photograph, so the camera does the Input job. The screen is used for Output.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: 'Compare the image to millions of examples it was trained on' is a job of which part?
options: Input
Processing
Output
Camera
questions.explanation: Comparing the image to trained examples is analysing with learned patterns, which is exactly what Processing does.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Which part identifies patterns like shape, colour, texture, or text?
options: Output
Screen
Processing
Input
questions.explanation: Finding patterns such as shape, colour, texture or text is Processing. Input only receives the image and Output only shows the result.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: 'Assign a confidence score to the best guess' belongs to which part?
options: Display
Output
Input
Processing
questions.explanation: The confidence score is part of deciding how sure the AI is about its guess, so it belongs to Processing.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: 'Decide what the photograph contains' is the job of which part?
options: Processing
Input
Output
Storage
questions.explanation: Deciding what the photo contains is the analysis step, so it is Processing. In the worksheet it was the odd one out in the Input column.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: What is a confidence score?
options: How many pixels the screen has
How sure the AI is of its guess
How clear the camera photo is
How many links the user is shown
questions.explanation: A confidence score shows how sure Processing is about its best guess. It is not about photo clarity, links or the screen.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Select the TWO Google Lens jobs that belong to the Processing part.
options: Format the result so the user can read it
Provide links to more information
Identify patterns like shape, colour, texture or text
Compare the image to millions of trained examples
Capture the photograph from the camera
questions.explanation: Identifying patterns and comparing to trained examples are Processing jobs. Capturing is Input; formatting results and providing links are Output.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Which of these does NOT belong to the Processing part?
options: Identify patterns like shape, colour or texture
Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Display the result on the screen
Compare the image to millions of examples
questions.explanation: Displaying the result is Output. In the worksheet it was the job to cross out in the Processing column; the other three are genuine Processing jobs.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: The Processing part compares the image to millions of examples it was trained on.
questions.explanation: True. Processing analyses the new image by comparing it with the millions of examples it learned from.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: The Processing part needs no training data because it decides by itself.
questions.explanation: False. Processing analyses input using patterns learned from training data; without training data it would have no patterns to use.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Which list contains ONLY patterns the Processing part might identify in an image?
options: Battery, signal, volume, brightness
Name, age, address, phone
Price, shop, bill, discount
Shape, colour, texture, text
questions.explanation: The worksheet lists shape, colour, texture and text as patterns Processing identifies. The other lists are phone settings or personal details, not image patterns.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: 'Re-analyse the photograph if the result is wrong' — which part would do this job?
options: Processing, because it analyses the input
Output, because it shows the result
Input, because it captures the photo
None; an AI never checks its work again
questions.explanation: Re-analysing means analysing again, which is Processing. In the worksheet this job was the odd one out placed in the Output column.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Why does Processing compare the new photo with millions of examples?
options: To ask the user which answer they prefer
To find which learned pattern it matches best
To make the photo brighter for the screen
To send the photo back to the camera
questions.explanation: Comparing with trained examples lets Processing find the pattern the photo matches best and decide what it contains.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: In the chapter's table, 'How the AI thinks about the input' is the description of…
options: Output
Design
Processing
Input
questions.explanation: The table describes Processing as how the AI thinks about the input, Input as what enters, and Output as what the user sees.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: A Processing part that learns the wrong patterns can still produce an answer that looks correct.
questions.explanation: True. The medical AI case study showed Processing learning camera styles instead of disease signs, yet its answers looked accurate during testing.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: A translation app turns a photographed menu into English. Which Processing job is most like 'recognising the letters in the photo'?
options: Capture the photograph from the camera
Format the result so the user can read it
Provide links to more information online
Identify patterns such as text and shape
questions.explanation: Recognising letters is identifying text patterns, a Processing job. Capturing is Input; formatting and links are Output.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: After deciding what the photo contains, what else does Processing attach to its best guess?
options: A confidence score
A list of web links
A camera flash setting
A readable layout
questions.explanation: Processing assigns a confidence score to its best guess. Links and readable layout are added by Output.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Google Lens says 'Rose – 60% confident'. Which part produced the 60%?
options: The camera
Processing
Input
Output
questions.explanation: The 60% is a confidence score, which Processing assigns to its best guess. Output only displays it.

questions.topic: Processing: Thinking with Patterns
questions.question: Select the TWO patterns the worksheet lists that Processing might identify in an image.
options: Taste
Time
Texture
Text
Temperature
questions.explanation: The worksheet lists shape, colour, texture and text. Temperature, taste and time cannot be read from a photograph's patterns.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: 'Show the identified object name on screen' is a job of which part?
options: Input
Processing
Output
Memory
questions.explanation: Showing the name on screen delivers the result to the user, which is Output's job.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: 'Provide links to more information' belongs to which part?
options: Input
Processing
Camera
Output
questions.explanation: Links are part of what the user sees at the end, so providing them is an Output job.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: 'Format the result so the user can read it' is the job of which part?
options: Output
Input
Training
Processing
questions.explanation: Formatting the result so the user can read it is delivering the result in an understandable way, which is Output.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Why does the Output part format the result?
options: So the AI can learn new patterns
So the user can understand it easily
So the camera can take a clearer photo
So Processing can compare more examples
questions.explanation: Output's whole purpose is to deliver the result in a way the user can understand, so formatting makes it readable.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Select the TWO jobs that belong to the Output part of Google Lens.
options: Compare the image to millions of examples
Capture the photograph from the camera
Show the identified object name on screen
Provide links to more information
Make sure the image is clear enough to use
questions.explanation: Showing the name and providing links are Output jobs. Checking clarity and capturing are Input; comparing is Processing.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Which of these does NOT belong to the Output part?
options: Provide links to more information online
Format the result so the user can read it
Re-analyse the photo if the result is wrong
Show the identified object name on screen
questions.explanation: Re-analysing the photo is analysis, so it is Processing. In the worksheet it was the job to cross out in the Output column.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: The Output part delivers the result in a way the user can understand.
questions.explanation: True. This is the worksheet's definition of Output: deliver the result in a way the user can understand.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: The Output part decides what the photograph contains.
questions.explanation: False. Deciding what the photo contains is Processing. Output only shows that decision to the user.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: A voice assistant speaks the weather forecast aloud. Which part is doing this?
options: Input
Processing
Training
Output
questions.explanation: Speaking the forecast delivers the result to the user, so it is Output, even though it uses sound instead of a screen.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Google Lens shows 'Tulsi plant' in big letters with a link to learn more. Which part(s) did this?
options: Output only
Input only
Processing only
Input and Processing
questions.explanation: Showing the name and providing a link are both Output jobs. Processing decided it was tulsi, but displaying that decision is Output.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Which phrase describes the Output part in the chapter's upgrade table?
options: Where the training data is kept
What the user sees at the end
What information enters AI
How the AI thinks about the input
questions.explanation: The table says Output is 'what the user sees at the end'. Input is what enters and Processing is how the AI thinks.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: If the Output shows the answer clearly, the Processing must have used the right patterns.
questions.explanation: False. The medical AI case study showed clear, accurate-looking outputs that came from Processing learning the wrong patterns.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: An Output-part problem, rather than an Input or Processing problem, would be:
options: The AI confused a mango leaf with a neem leaf
The AI was trained mostly on foreign plants
The answer is shown in tiny text nobody can read
The camera photo is far too dark to use
questions.explanation: Unreadable text is a failure to deliver the result understandably, so it is Output. A dark photo is Input; confusion and poor training are Processing.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Which part would 'display the result on the screen'?
options: Processing
Input
Camera
Output
questions.explanation: Displaying the result is Output. In the worksheet this job was wrongly placed in the Processing column and had to be crossed out.

questions.topic: Output: Showing the Result
questions.question: Google Lens shows a link 'Learn more about Tulsi'. Which Output job is this?
options: Provide links to more information
Show the identified object name
Format the result so it is readable
Assign a confidence score
questions.explanation: A 'learn more' link is the Output job 'provide links to more information'. Assigning a confidence score is Processing, not Output.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the worksheet's Input column, which job should be crossed out because it belongs to Processing?
options: Make sure the image is clear enough to use
Decide what the photograph contains
Capture the photograph from the camera
Pass the image data to the next part
questions.explanation: Deciding what the photo contains is analysis, a Processing job. Capturing, checking clarity and passing data on are genuine Input jobs.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the Processing column, which job should be crossed out because it is really an Output job?
options: Identify patterns like shape and colour
Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Display the result on the screen
Compare the image to millions of examples
questions.explanation: Displaying the result is Output. Comparing, identifying patterns and assigning a confidence score are all Processing.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the Output column, which job should be crossed out because it belongs to Processing?
options: Show the identified object name on screen
Provide links to more information online
Format the result so the user can read it
Re-analyse the photograph if the result is wrong
questions.explanation: Re-analysing is Processing. Showing the name, providing links and formatting the result are all Output jobs.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Sort it: 'Capture the photograph from the camera'.
options: Input
Processing
Output
Training
questions.explanation: Capturing the photo brings information into the system, so it is Input.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Sort it: 'Format the result so the user can read it'.
options: Processing
Output
Input
Training
questions.explanation: Formatting the result for the user is delivering it understandably, so it is Output.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Sort it: 'Identify patterns like shape, colour, texture, or text'.
options: Input
Output
Processing
Training
questions.explanation: Identifying patterns is analysing the input, so it is Processing.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Select the TWO jobs that belong to the SAME part.
options: Provide links to more information
Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Make sure the image is clear enough to use
Pass the image data to the next part
questions.explanation: Checking clarity and passing data on are both Input jobs. Providing links is Output and assigning a confidence score is Processing.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Select the TWO jobs that belong to the Processing part.
options: Show the identified object name on screen
Capture the photograph from the camera
Decide what the photograph contains
Re-analyse the photograph if the result is wrong
questions.explanation: Deciding contents and re-analysing are both analysis, so Processing. Showing the name is Output; capturing is Input.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Which pair puts BOTH jobs in the wrong part?
options: Input: capture the photo; Processing: assign a confidence score
Processing: identify patterns; Output: provide links
Input: pass the image data on; Output: format the result
Input: decide what the photo contains; Output: compare to examples
questions.explanation: Deciding contents and comparing to examples are both Processing jobs, so putting them under Input and Output is doubly wrong. The other pairs are correctly placed.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: 'Display the result on the screen' and 'Show the identified object name on screen' both belong to Output.
questions.explanation: True. Both deliver the result to the user on the screen, which is Output's job, even though the worksheet listed one of them in the wrong column.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the worksheet, every Google Lens job was already listed under the correct part, so nothing needed crossing out.
questions.explanation: False. Each column had one job that did not belong there and had to be crossed out, such as 'Decide what the photograph contains' under Input.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the worksheet, what were you asked to do with a job that does NOT belong to a part?
options: Cross it out
Tick it
Circle it twice
Underline it
questions.explanation: The instruction was to tick the responsibilities that belong to a part and cross out the one that does not.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: In the worksheet, what mark shows a job that DOES belong to a part?
options: A question mark
A tick ✓
A cross ✗
A star
questions.explanation: Jobs that belong to a part get a tick; the one that does not belong gets a cross.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: 'Assign a confidence score' and 'Make sure the image is clear' belong to:
options: Both to Processing
Both to Output
Processing and Input, in that order
Input and Processing, in that order
questions.explanation: Assigning a confidence score is Processing; making sure the image is clear is Input. Neither is Output.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Which job happens LAST in Google Lens's flow?
options: Capture the photograph from the camera
Compare the image to millions of examples
Make sure the image is clear enough to use
Format the result so the user can read it
questions.explanation: Formatting the result is an Output job, and Output comes last. Capturing and checking clarity are Input (first); comparing is Processing (middle).

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Which job happens FIRST in Google Lens's flow?
options: Capture the photograph from the camera
Assign a confidence score to the best guess
Show the identified object name on screen
Compare the image to millions of examples
questions.explanation: Capturing the photo is Input, which comes first. Scoring and comparing are Processing; showing the name is Output.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: A classmate ticks 'Provide links to more information' under Processing. What should you tell them?
options: Links are not part of any AI system
Links are shown to the user, so that is Output
Links come from the camera, so that is Input
They are right; Processing provides the links
questions.explanation: Providing links is part of what the user sees at the end, so it is Output, not Processing.

questions.topic: Sorting Jobs: Which Part Does What
questions.question: Which job is sometimes mistaken for Output but is really Processing, because it analyses rather than displays?
options: Provide links to more information online
Format the result so the user can read it
Re-analyse the photograph if the result is wrong
Show the identified object name on screen
questions.explanation: Re-analysing is analysis, so it is Processing even though it happens after a result appears. The other three genuinely display things to the user.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: What problem with Google Lens does the worksheet describe?
options: It runs out of battery too quickly in hot weather
It cannot take clear photographs in dim light
It shows results only in English, never Hindi
It struggles to identify Indian plants and local food
questions.explanation: The worksheet's 'Google Lens problem' is that it struggles to identify Indian plants and local food correctly.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: According to the worksheet, WHY does Google Lens struggle with Indian plants and food?
options: Its training data came mostly from outside India
Its camera lens cannot focus on green leaves
Its screen is too small to show Indian names
Its users forgot to switch on mobile internet
questions.explanation: The worksheet says its processing was trained mostly on data from outside India, so it lacks patterns for Indian plants and food.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Which part most needs upgrading to fix the Indian plants and food problem?
options: The battery
Processing
Input
Output
questions.explanation: The cause is training data from outside India, which affects how the AI thinks about the input. That is Processing.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: What specific change would most directly fix the problem?
options: Add many more links to foreign websites
Make the camera shutter click much faster
Train it on many Indian plant and food photos
Give the phone a bigger, brighter screen
questions.explanation: Since the problem is missing Indian examples in training, adding many Indian plant and food images to the training data targets the real cause.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Google Lens's trouble with Indian food is mainly a Processing problem, not a camera problem.
questions.explanation: True. The worksheet blames the processing being trained mostly on data from outside India, not the camera.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Upgrading the Output part by using bigger text would fix Google Lens's trouble recognising Indian plants.
questions.explanation: False. Bigger text only changes how the result is shown. The wrong recognition happens in Processing because of its training data.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: A student upgrades the Input part with a sharper camera. Why will this NOT fully fix the Indian food problem?
options: Sharper cameras make photos too large to send
The Output part cannot display sharper photos
Indian food cannot be photographed clearly
The Processing still lacks patterns for Indian food
questions.explanation: A sharper photo is still analysed by a Processing part that never learned Indian food patterns, so the wrong guesses continue.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: The worksheet asks: 'What new problem could your upgrade accidentally cause?' Why is this question included?
options: Because a fix in one place can cause new mistakes
Because upgrades are never allowed in AI systems
Because the user must pay for every upgrade
Because Google Lens cannot be changed at all
questions.explanation: Changing one part can have side effects, so good designers think ahead about what new problem their upgrade might create.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: If Processing is retrained ONLY on Indian examples, what new problem could appear?
options: The Input part will no longer pass data on
It may get worse at foods from other countries
The camera will stop taking any photographs
The screen will refuse to show any results
questions.explanation: Training only on Indian examples could leave Processing with weaker patterns for other countries' plants and foods, a new problem caused by the upgrade.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are true about the Google Lens India problem.
options: The best fix is to remove the Output part
It only happens when the phone is offline
It is caused by training data mostly from outside India
The best fix is in the Processing part
It is caused by Indian phones having weak cameras
questions.explanation: The worksheet says the cause is training data from outside India, which points to upgrading Processing. Cameras, Output and being offline are not the cause.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: In the upgrade table, Input is described as:
options: What the user sees at the end
Where the upgrade is paid for
What information enters AI
How the AI thinks about the input
questions.explanation: The table describes Input as 'what information enters AI'. The other two phrases describe Processing and Output.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Which upgrade targets the OUTPUT part?
options: Collect photos of Indian street food
Add a better lens to the phone camera
Learn patterns from Indian plant photos
Show plant names in local Indian languages
questions.explanation: Showing names in local languages changes what the user sees at the end, so it is an Output upgrade. The others target Input or Processing.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Which upgrade targets the INPUT part?
options: Let users take clearer close-up leaf photos
Train on millions of Indian food images
Show results with Hindi and Tamil names
Give a confidence score for each guess
questions.explanation: Clearer close-up photos change the information entering the AI, so it is an Input upgrade. Training is Processing; showing names is Output.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: An upgrade can fix the problem it targets and still accidentally create a different one.
questions.explanation: True. That is why the worksheet asks what new problem your upgrade could accidentally cause.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Google Lens correctly names a pizza but calls a dosa a 'pancake'. Which explanation best fits the chapter?
options: Dosas and pizzas are the same food to everyone
Processing saw far more pizzas than dosas in training
The Output part prefers Italian names for food
The camera cannot photograph round flat foods
questions.explanation: Training data mostly from outside India gives Processing strong patterns for pizza and weak ones for dosa, so it falls back on a similar-looking foreign food.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: The upgrade activity's worksheet level was called:
options: Thinking deeper
Learning is fun
Powering up
Laying the tracks
questions.explanation: Question 2, the upgrade activity, is at the 'Powering up' level. 'Laying the tracks' is Q1 and 'Thinking deeper' is Q3.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Which question is NOT one the upgrade table asks you to answer?
options: Why does this part need upgrading most?
What specific change would you make?
What new problem could your upgrade cause?
How much will the upgrade cost in rupees?
questions.explanation: The table asks why the part needs upgrading, what specific change you would make, and what new problem it could cause. Cost is not asked.

questions.topic: Upgrading Google Lens for India
questions.question: Select the TWO upgrade questions the worksheet asks.
options: How many users does Google Lens have?
Which colour should the app icon be?
Why does this part need upgrading most?
What new problem could your upgrade cause?
questions.explanation: The upgrade table asks why the part needs upgrading most, what change you would make, and what new problem could result. User numbers and icon colour are not asked.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: In the 'Thinking deeper' task, what kind of problem should your AI system solve?
options: A real problem from daily life in India
A puzzle from a fantasy video game
A maths sum copied from the textbook
A problem that only computers face
questions.explanation: The task asks you to choose a real problem from daily life in India that AI could help solve.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Which format could your design take, according to the task?
options: A spoken speech without any notes
A slide, poster or short document
A long novel with many chapters
A music video with lots of dancing
questions.explanation: The task says to create one digital slide, poster, or short document.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: What is a 'failure mode' in your AI design?
options: The name you decide to give your AI system
The number of slides in your presentation
Which part could fail and why that matters to users
The colour scheme chosen for your poster
questions.explanation: The task defines a failure mode as which part could fail, what could go wrong, and why that would matter to users.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Select the TWO things the design task says you must include.
options: A list of competing apps
The names of your teammates
The specific job of the Input part and why it matters
One likely failure mode
The price of the AI system
questions.explanation: The design must include the job of each part (Input, Processing, Output), one likely failure mode and a reflection. Price, competitors and teammates are not required.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: The 'Reflection' point asks you to explain how learning about the inside of AI changes…
options: How quickly your phone battery charges up
How much mobile data costs in India today
How many apps you keep installed on your phone
How you think about using tools like Google Lens
questions.explanation: The reflection asks how learning about the inside of AI systems changes the way you think about using tools like Google Lens.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: An AI reads bus timetables for passengers in India. Which is an INPUT failure mode?
options: A faded, torn timetable photo gives little to work with
The AI mixes up two bus numbers it learned together
The result is read out too fast to understand
The AI is trained only on timetables from Delhi
questions.explanation: A poor photo is bad information entering the system, so it is an Input failure. Mixing up numbers and Delhi-only training are Processing; a too-fast read-out is Output.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Same bus-timetable AI. Which is a PROCESSING failure mode?
options: The screen brightness is set too low
It learned patterns only from Delhi timetables
The camera on the passenger's phone is cracked
The spoken result is in the wrong language
questions.explanation: Learning only Delhi patterns affects how the AI thinks about the input, so it is Processing. A cracked camera is Input; wrong language and dim screen are Output.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Same AI. Which is an OUTPUT failure mode?
options: The photo of the timetable is blurry
It was trained on too few timetables
It shows the time in a font too small to read
It confuses bus number 42 with bus number 24
questions.explanation: A font too small to read fails to deliver the result understandably, so it is Output. Confusing numbers and too little training are Processing; a blurry photo is Input.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: The design task says you should pick a problem from daily life in another country.
questions.explanation: False. The task asks for a real problem from daily life in India.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: In your design, a failure mode should name which part could fail and why that would matter to users.
questions.explanation: True. The task describes a failure mode as which part could fail, what could go wrong, and why that would matter to users.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Why does the task ask 'why that would matter to users' for a failure mode?
options: Because users must pay money for every failure
Because failures make the poster look nicer
Because users design the training data
Because real people are affected when a part fails
questions.explanation: AI systems are used by real people, so a failure in any part has real consequences for them. Thinking about users keeps the design responsible.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: The third worksheet level was called:
options: Thinking deeper
Laying the tracks
Powering up
Learning is fun
questions.explanation: Question 3, the design task, is at the 'Thinking deeper (at your own pace)' level.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: A crop-disease AI for farmers. Which failure would matter MOST to a farmer?
options: The farmer's phone case is slightly scratched
Processing wrongly marks a healthy crop as diseased
The app icon uses a dull shade of green
The app's name is hard for farmers to spell
questions.explanation: A wrong diagnosis could make a farmer spray or destroy a healthy crop, a real harm. Icon colour, name and phone case do not change the result.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: The three worksheet levels, in order, are 'Laying the tracks', 'Powering up' and 'Thinking deeper'.
questions.explanation: True. Q1 is 'Laying the tracks', Q2 is 'Powering up' and Q3 is 'Thinking deeper (at your own pace)'.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: Which of these daily-life problems would fit the task's instruction best?
options: Deciding which movie star is the most famous
Guessing the winning lottery numbers for tomorrow
Helping farmers spot crop diseases from leaf photos
Choosing the strongest dragon for a fantasy game
questions.explanation: The task asks for a real problem from daily life in India that AI could help solve. Spotting crop diseases is real and useful; the others are not.

questions.topic: Designing an AI System and Its Failure Modes
questions.question: In the design task, the 'Problem' point asks you to state:
options: The problems with your classmates' AI
The problem with Google's business
The problem of charging your phone
The problem your AI system solves
questions.explanation: The first bullet of the task is 'the problem your AI system solves'.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: In which year did researchers find the hidden problem in the medical AI system?
questions.explanation: The case study says that in 2018 researchers found a hidden problem inside a medical AI system.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What did the medical AI system detect diseases from?
options: Voice recordings
Eye photographs
Chest X-rays
Blood samples
questions.explanation: The AI detected diseases from eye (retinal) photographs.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What was the INPUT of the medical AI system?
options: Lists of medicines each patient was given
Videos of patients walking in the clinic
Retinal photographs from different hospitals
Doctors' handwritten notes about patients
questions.explanation: The case study states: 'Input: retinal photographs from different hospitals.'

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Besides signs of disease, what ELSE did the AI learn to recognise?
options: Patients' names and home addresses
The weather on the day of the photo
The doctor who took each photograph
Hospital camera styles and equipment
questions.explanation: Instead of learning only the signs of disease, the AI also learned to recognise hospital camera styles and equipment.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What was the AI partly guessing instead of just the disease?
options: Where the image came from
How old the patient was
Which medicine to prescribe
How expensive the camera was
questions.explanation: The AI was partly guessing where the image came from (which hospital), not just what disease it showed.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What name do researchers give to this problem?
options: Slow learning
Shortcut learning
Deep learning
Long-cut learning
questions.explanation: Researchers call this problem shortcut learning: the AI finds an easy clue that works for the wrong reason.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What was the OUTPUT of the medical AI like during testing?
options: Blank screens with no result
Photos sent back to the hospital
Diagnoses that looked accurate
Diagnoses that were always wrong
questions.explanation: The output was a diagnosis that looked accurate during testing but became less reliable at new hospitals.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What happened to the AI's reliability at NEW hospitals?
options: It became more reliable
It stayed exactly the same
It stopped working entirely
It became less reliable
questions.explanation: The diagnosis became less reliable at new hospitals because the camera-style clues it had learned no longer matched.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Why did the AI become less reliable at new hospitals?
options: Different cameras broke its camera-style shortcut
They had no patients with any eye disease at all
They refused to photograph any patients' eyes
They used a completely different AI system
questions.explanation: The AI had partly learned hospital camera styles. At new hospitals with different equipment, that shortcut no longer pointed to the right answer.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Which part of the medical AI system had the hidden problem?
options: The camera
Processing
Input
Output
questions.explanation: The case study says that even when Input and Output seem correct, the Processing part can still learn the wrong patterns, and that is what happened here.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: The medical AI system's Input and Output both seemed correct during testing.
questions.explanation: True. The photographs were fine and the diagnoses looked accurate; the hidden problem was in Processing.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: The problem in the medical AI was found in the Output part, which displayed the wrong diagnosis.
questions.explanation: False. The Output looked correct during testing. The problem was that Processing had learned the wrong patterns (camera styles).

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Shortcut learning means the Processing part learns the wrong patterns even though it gives correct-looking answers.
questions.explanation: True. The AI's answers looked accurate in testing, but it had partly learned camera clues instead of only disease signs.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Because the medical AI gave accurate answers during testing, its Processing must have learned only the signs of disease.
questions.explanation: False. This is exactly the trap: accurate-looking answers hid the fact that Processing had also learned hospital camera styles.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are true about the 2018 medical AI.
options: It detected diseases from X-rays of the chest
It had a broken Output part
It used retinal photographs from different hospitals
It also learned to recognise hospital camera styles
It was tested only on one hospital's patients and never failed
questions.explanation: Its input was retinal photographs from different hospitals and its Processing learned camera styles. It did fail at new hospitals, used eye photos not X-rays, and its Output was not broken.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What does the case study prove about checking an AI system?
options: Only the Input part ever needs to be checked carefully
Medical AIs never make mistakes once they pass testing
Correct Input and Output do not prove correct Processing
If the Output is correct, the whole system is correct
questions.explanation: The chapter's lesson is that even when Input and Output seem correct, Processing can still have learned the wrong patterns.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: What is a 'shortcut' in shortcut learning?
options: A faster camera that snaps photos very quickly
A quicker road between two different hospitals
A smaller screen that loads results faster
An easy clue that works for the wrong reason
questions.explanation: The shortcut was the camera style: an easy clue that happened to match the answer in testing but had nothing to do with the disease itself.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: The heading calls it 'the AI that gave correct answers — for the wrong reasons'. What were the 'wrong reasons'?
options: Camera and hospital clues, not disease signs
Hints whispered by the patients' doctors
Answers copied from a medical textbook
Random guesses with no pattern at all
questions.explanation: The AI used hospital camera styles and equipment as clues, which have nothing to do with the disease, so its correct answers rested on the wrong reasons.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Where was the research about this problem published?
options: Indian Express
PLOS Medicine
Google Lens Blog
A school textbook
questions.explanation: The source given is a PLOS Medicine journal article.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: A school AI grades essays. It learned that longer essays got high marks, so it gives high marks to any long essay. This is most like…
options: An Output problem with small text
A problem only with the student's handwriting
Shortcut learning in the medical AI
An Input problem with a blurry camera
questions.explanation: Like the medical AI using camera styles, the essay AI uses length as an easy clue instead of the real quality of the writing. That is shortcut learning.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: The medical AI worked better at new hospitals because it had seen more camera styles.
questions.explanation: False. It became less reliable at new hospitals because the camera styles there did not match the shortcut it had learned.

questions.topic: Case Study: Shortcut Learning in Medical AI
questions.question: Select the TWO things that were TRUE of the medical AI's Processing part.
options: It learned patients' names
It learned the doctors' voices
It learned signs of disease
It learned hospital camera styles
questions.explanation: The AI learned the signs of disease but also learned camera styles and equipment. Names and voices were not part of the eye photographs.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: What big question does the chapter ask about looking inside AI?
options: How to make AI apps on phones load much faster
How much popular AI products cost for a family
How to take better photographs with a phone camera
How knowing what is inside AI changes our trust in it
questions.explanation: The worksheet opens with: 'How does knowing what happens inside AI change the way we trust its answers?'

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: According to the chapter, how should knowing the three parts change our trust in AI answers?
options: We judge answers knowing where they could fail
We trust every single AI answer completely
We stop using any AI tools altogether
We trust only what the Output part shows
questions.explanation: Knowing the parts lets us ask which part might have failed and judge each answer wisely, rather than blindly trusting or rejecting AI.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Google Lens gives an answer with a low confidence score. Knowing the inside of AI, a careful user would…
options: Believe it because AI is always right
Double-check before trusting the result
Trust it because the screen looked clear
Assume the camera must be broken
questions.explanation: A low confidence score means Processing is unsure, so a careful user checks the answer another way before relying on it.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: A confident-looking Output means the answer is definitely correct.
questions.explanation: False. The medical AI's outputs looked accurate yet came from wrong patterns. A neat display does not prove the Processing was right.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: If an AI's answer is wrong, which parts might be responsible?
options: Only the Input part of the system
Only the person holding the phone
Any of Input, Processing or Output
Only the Output part of the system
questions.explanation: A bad photo (Input), wrong patterns (Processing) or an unclear display (Output) can each cause a wrong or misleading answer.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Select the TWO lessons the chapter teaches about trusting AI.
options: Only Output errors matter to users
Trust grows when the screen is bigger
Check which part may have failed instead of blaming the whole AI
Correct-looking results can still come from wrong patterns
AI answers should never be questioned
questions.explanation: The chapter teaches us to think about which part failed and warns, through the medical AI story, that correct-looking results can hide wrong patterns.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Which statement best shows someone who understands the inside of an AI system?
options: 'It is on the screen, so it must be completely true.'
'The phone is brand new, so the AI must be right.'
'AI never ever makes mistakes with photographs.'
'It may be wrong if its training data was different.'
questions.explanation: Linking a possible mistake to the training data shows understanding of Processing. The other statements trust the screen or the phone instead of the parts.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Why is a wrong answer from Processing hard to spot just by looking at the Output?
options: The Output can look clear even when it is wrong
The Output always shows an error message
The Output is usually hidden from the user
Processing never produces wrong answers
questions.explanation: Output formats whatever Processing decides, so a wrong decision can still be displayed neatly and confidently.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: The chapter uses which real app as its main example?
options: WhatsApp
Google Lens
Google Maps
YouTube
questions.explanation: Google Lens, which identifies objects from photographs, is the example used in both worksheet activities.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Knowing the inside of AI means we should distrust every AI answer completely.
questions.explanation: False. The aim is to trust wisely: understand which part could fail and check when needed, not to reject every answer.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: A user says: 'Lens was wrong about my tulsi plant, so the camera is bad.' What is the better explanation from the chapter?
options: The Input part refused to take a photo
Tulsi plants cannot be photographed well
Processing lacked patterns for Indian plants
The screen was too dim to show the plant
questions.explanation: The worksheet explains that Google Lens struggles with Indian plants because its processing was trained mostly on data from outside India, not because of the camera.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Which habit shows wise use of an AI tool after this chapter?
options: Never read the result the AI shows
Use the AI only late at night time
Delete the app after one error
Ask which part might have gone wrong
questions.explanation: Understanding Input, Processing and Output lets you ask which part failed when a result looks odd, instead of overreacting or ignoring it.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: The design task asks for a 'Reflection'. Which reflection best matches the chapter's goal?
options: Knowing the parts helps me judge when to trust Lens
Knowing the parts makes Lens take better photos
Knowing the parts lets me skip reading results
Knowing the parts makes the app free to use
questions.explanation: The reflection should explain how understanding the inside of AI changes how you think about using tools like Google Lens, especially how much to trust them.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: Even a correct final answer could have come from the wrong patterns inside Processing.
questions.explanation: True. The medical AI gave correct answers for the wrong reasons, which is why researchers call it shortcut learning.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: After this chapter, which is the WEAKEST reason to trust an AI answer?
options: The confidence score was high and checked by a person
The answer appeared quickly on a bright screen
The Processing was trained on data like my case
The Input photo was clear and complete
questions.explanation: Speed and a bright screen say nothing about Input quality or Processing patterns. The other reasons relate to the parts that actually decide the answer.

questions.topic: Trust: Why Looking Inside AI Matters
questions.question: The three-part model (Input, Processing, Output) can be used to think about many AI tools, not only Google Lens.
questions.explanation: True. The design task asks you to apply Input, Processing and Output to your own AI system for a daily-life problem in India.
